note: Typical sizes and friction coefficients used only when the question does not state them. Every scene receipt names which values were defaults. Not outcomes: outcomes come from the solver.

sources.friction: Engineering ToolBox, Friction and Friction Coefficients, https://www.engineeringtoolbox.com/friction-coefficients-d_778.html (mid-range of the listed static coefficients; table = plastic or glass on finished wood, ~0.2-0.3)
sources.sizes: typical consumer-object dimensions (500 mL PET bottle ~ 0.22 m x 0.065 m, ~0.5 kg filled; FIFA size-5 ball r 0.11 m, 0.43 kg); approximate, labelled default in every receipt

push.note: FORGE push convention: a steady horizontal force at the stated point, 1.25 x the smallest force that would start the body moving on the reference table either way (static friction mu_table m g, or tipping about the front edge m g w/2 / h), so the same push is applied on every surface, for 0.5 s; stated in every receipt. The solver decides which way it moves.

materials.note: Bulk densities in kg/m3. A row is used only when its two handbook figures agree within 15 percent. A record that names a wood and a metal is a wood shell plus a metal frame (four corner posts of the board section, plus one face plate of the board thickness), not the wood alone. A bulk solid (stone, glass, ceramic) uses the bounding-box volume. Fabric's two figures do not agree, so fabric is not used.

sources.usda: USDA Forest Products Laboratory Wood Handbook, wood densities at about 12 percent moisture
sources.asm: ASM Handbook, typical densities of commercial metals
sources.crc: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, densities of solids

fluids.note: Fluid densities in kg/m3 near room temperature. Used only when the two figures agree within 15 percent.

sources.nist: NIST Chemistry WebBook, fluid densities at 1 atm near 20-25 C

thermal.note: Specific heat in J/kg/K and phase-change temperatures in C. A row is used only when each pair agrees within 15 percent (temperatures within 1 degree when the point is 0).

sources.toolbox: Engineering ToolBox, specific heat and boiling/melting points
